slides.title: Uncovering the Truth Behind Warfare
slides.text: Why Military History Is Biased And Broken
slides.speech: A survey of 163 American historians proved that political bias directly alters how military conflicts are recorded and taught. While military history has massive public appeal, major universities treat it as an academic orphan. Scholars struggle with hidden records, like the completely lost chemical formula for ancient Greek fire, and the deliberate destruction of files in modern Iraqi campaigns. On top of that, historians must fight internal biases like Eurocentricity and the isolation of land, sea, and air analysis. Despite the Society for Military History growing to twenty-three hundred members since 1937, the field remains a battleground of political perspectives.
